reviewer: internal-medicine physician on the study team
form: item by item: a 1-9 score for every Part A action, a harmful / equivocal / not harmful verdict for every Part B option with each plan statement marked stated, hedged or not stated, and ok / concern for every Part C instruction; notes are the reviewer's own

supersedes.statement: all of the responses are appropriate
supersedes.form: one overall verdict covering every item of every part, not per-item 1-9 ratings
supersedes.why: the overall verdict gave no per-item scores, so the review was repeated item by item on the same page and key; this file replaces it

A.question: Is this unlisted plan action appropriate for this patient (RAND-UCLA 1-9)?
A.blinding: model, instruction and AI-rater flag status hidden

notes.A005: Urinalysis is an appropriate, low-burden component of unexplained iron-deficiency anemia evaluation to identify urinary blood loss. A negative result would not end the GI or renal-tract assessment. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8515119/
notes.A006: Reviewing AV-nodal-blocking drugs and following the first-degree AV block is reasonable. Relevant calcium-channel blockers are verapamil and diltiazem; the conduction finding should not distract from evaluating exertional chest pain. Source: https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000628
notes.A007: Renal and hepatic safety tests are not routinely required solely for an HIV exposure when no antiretroviral prophylaxis is prescribed. They may become appropriate for PrEP selection or other clinical indications; HIV, hepatitis, STI and pregnancy assessment remain separate considerations. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/rr/rr7401a1.htm
notes.A008: Optional hepatitis A immunity testing is low risk but has no clear indication from this isolated vaginal exposure. Routine HAV screening or prevaccination serology is not recommended; testing can be individualized when prior immunity would change vaccination decisions. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/hepatitis-a/hcp/diagnosis-testing/index.html
notes.A009: The conditional low-dose proposal and close monitoring reduce concern, but ongoing unintended weight loss and low-normal BMI make another GLP-1 agent an unfavorable default. First assess nutrition and the cause of weight loss, discuss weight-neutral alternatives or insulin when indicated, and make any GLP-1 trial an individualized decision. Source: https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S277/163949/13-Older-Adults-Standards-of-Care-in-Diabetes
notes.A011: Switching the route does not establish safety after a stated grade 3 nivolumab infusion reaction. The nivolumab label recommends discontinuation for severe reactions; subcutaneous nivolumab is not an established workaround. Any exceptional further exposure would require oncology/allergy assessment and a specifically justified protocol. Source: https://dailymed.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f570b9c4-6846-4de2-abfa-4d0a4ae4e394
notes.A012: A negative workup does not make a slow graded infusion safe after a grade 3 reaction. Label guidance recommends discontinuation; simply starting at 25% of the rate is not equivalent to a specialist-led desensitization protocol. Exceptional rechallenge requires a much stronger risk assessment and safeguards. Source: https://dailymed.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f570b9c4-6846-4de2-abfa-4d0a4ae4e394
notes.A013: A broad pituitary panel is not supported by stable isolated mild thrombocytopenia and a remote postpartum hemorrhage alone. First confirm the platelet abnormality and assess standard secondary causes; pituitary testing becomes appropriate if history or examination suggests postpartum hypopituitarism. Source: https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2019000812
notes.A021: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg weekly is a valid starting dose, but continued GLP-1 therapy may worsen unwanted weight loss at BMI 19.7. The switch must explicitly discontinue semaglutide and include nutrition/weight monitoring; the conditional proposal is therefore equivocal as written. Source: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=463050bd-2b1c-40f5-b3c3-0a04bb433309
notes.A025: A one-time immunoglobulin panel can be reasonable during specialist evaluation for suspected immune thrombocytopenia. Stable counts above 100k and no recurrent infections make its yield uncertain here, so this is optional rather than a routine requirement. Source: https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2019000812
notes.A026: An explicitly nonoverlapping, low-dose switch can be considered after shared decision-making, but dulaglutide can also reduce appetite and weight. Ongoing unexplained weight loss requires assessment and close monitoring, and a weight-neutral regimen may fit the stated goal better. Source: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=463050bd-2b1c-40f5-b3c3-0a04bb433309
notes.A028: Genetic assessment is reasonable if a significant adenoma burden or a convincing hereditary cancer history emerges. These triggers are not established in this case, and an unspecified young relative with polyps alone is too broad a criterion for automatic referral. Source: https://webfiles.gi.org/GuidelineHighlights/polyposis-highlights.pdf
notes.A029: The supplied history provides no dyspnea, edema, orthopnea or examination findings suggesting heart failure. Routine BNP adds little to this recurrent postinfectious cough evaluation; it becomes appropriate if cardiac features are identified. Source: https://publications.ersnet.org/index.php/content/erj/55/1/1901136
notes.A030: Routine skin or in-vitro sulfonamide testing is not well validated, so avoiding it is reasonable. Urticaria supports suspected hypersensitivity rather than proving its mechanism, and the associated AKI needs separate assessment for drug-induced nephritis before any future exposure. Source: https://www.aaaai.org/Aaaai/media/Media-Library-PDFs/Allergist%20Resources/Statements%20and%20Practice%20Parameters/Drug-Allergy-PP-9-2022.pdf
notes.A032: Routine total IgE is nonspecific and is not supported by the supplied recurrent cough history alone. Complete spirometry and a directed assessment first; allergy or ABPA-related testing should follow relevant clinical findings. Source: https://publications.ersnet.org/index.php/content/erj/55/1/1901136
notes.A033: Allergy-supervised graded challenge is a reasonable conditional option if TMP-SMX is genuinely needed and the prior AKI is convincingly unrelated to hypersensitivity. Drug-induced nephritis or another severe delayed reaction must be excluded; waiting several weeks alone does not establish safety. Source: https://www.aaaai.org/Aaaai/media/Media-Library-PDFs/Allergist%20Resources/Statements%20and%20Practice%20Parameters/Drug-Allergy-PP-9-2022.pdf
notes.A034: Total IgE is not a routine diagnostic test for recurrent postinfectious cough without evidence of atopy, asthma or another specific indication. Spirometry and directed evaluation of common cough causes are more informative. Source: https://publications.ersnet.org/index.php/content/erj/55/1/1901136
notes.A035: Severe documented iron deficiency already explains the anemia and fatigue. TSH is a low-priority optional test unless additional history, examination findings or persistent symptoms after iron repletion suggest thyroid disease; it should not distract from treating and investigating the iron deficiency. Source: https://doi.org/10.1136/GUTJNL-2021-325210
notes.A036: Baseline immunoglobulins may be reasonable in a specialist workup for suspected immune thrombocytopenia, but stable counts above 100k do not establish ITP. Mild hand eczema without recurrent infections does not by itself justify an immune-deficiency diagnosis or make this test mandatory. Source: https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2019000812
notes.A037: Albuterol may help documented bronchospasm, which is not described here. It does not address pneumonitis or infection; the persistent symptoms, tree-in-bud changes and prior positive TB test require prompt diagnostic reassessment rather than reliance on a bronchodilator. Source: https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.21.01440
notes.A039: BIC/FTC/TAF for 28 days is a current preferred PEP regimen when exposure is within 72 hours. That condition is not met in the stated case, so it is a timing-dependent contingency only; if eligible, draw baseline tests but do not delay the first dose for results. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/rr/rr7401a1.htm
notes.A040: Recent ferritin below 5 and low transferrin saturation already establish iron deficiency. Repeating them as a prerequisite to any iron adds little and may delay needed treatment; repeat studies should answer a specific uncertainty or monitor response. Source: https://doi.org/10.1136/GUTJNL-2021-325210
notes.A044: Deferring the anticoagulation decision until the entire embolic-source workup is complete may leave a new renal infarct untreated. Urgently assess infarct timing, mechanism and bleeding risk while investigating the source in parallel; anticoagulation is not universal for every infarct mechanism. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30215794/
notes.A045: Avoiding routine ischemia testing may be reasonable after a resolved low-risk episode, but negative troponin and normal TSH do not exclude an arrhythmia. Confirm the ED ECG and symptom course; recurrent or unexplained palpitations can warrant ambulatory monitoring before categorically excluding further cardiac evaluation. Source: https://www.hrsonline.org/resource/2017-ishne-hrs-expert-consensus-statement/
notes.A046: The symmetric palm/sole erythema, fissuring and pain during capecitabine strongly suggest hand-foot syndrome. Uric acid and inflammatory markers have limited routine yield for that diagnosis; reserve them for examination findings suggesting an additional inflammatory or crystal arthritis and do not delay oncology review. Source: https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/hair-skin-and-nails/1416-hand-foot-syndrome-associated-with-chemothera
notes.A047: A one-time immunoglobulin panel can be reasonable during specialist evaluation for suspected immune thrombocytopenia. Stable counts above 100k, no recurrent infections and mild eczema alone make its yield uncertain; it is optional rather than clearly required in this presentation. Source: https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2019000812
notes.A048: HAV IgG is not a routine test required by this HIV exposure. Prevaccination testing can be useful when prior natural immunity is likely or testing is cost-effective, but being unvaccinated alone does not establish that need and testing should not delay indicated vaccination. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/hepatitis-a/hcp/diagnosis-testing/index.html
notes.A050: This is a preferred 28-day PEP regimen, but benefit from starting beyond 72 hours is unproven and routine late initiation is not recommended. Specialist-directed exceptions require individualized exposure timing and risk assessment; pregnancy is not itself a contraindication to indicated PEP. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/rr/rr7401a1.htm
notes.A051: A negative stress test and low preventive ASCVD score do not categorically exclude obstructive CAD in a patient with exertional chest pain and dyspnea. Review test adequacy and symptom persistence; CCTA can be reasonable if clinical suspicion remains, although immediate invasive angiography is not automatically indicated. Source: https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2021.07.053
notes.A054: Baseline QTc assessment is appropriate before clinically justified long-term macrolide therapy or when relevant cardiac risks exist. An ECG is not a routine diagnostic test for this recurrent cough and should not imply that repeated empiric azithromycin is indicated. Source: https://doi.org/10.1136/thoraxjnl-2019-213929
notes.A057: Erectile dysfunction does not make macroprolactin testing inappropriate. With only mild persistent prolactin elevation, checking biologically active monomeric prolactin can help avoid an incorrect prolactinoma diagnosis or unnecessary imaging; clinical symptoms alone do not reliably exclude macroprolactinemia. Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41574-023-00886-5
notes.A058: Nivolumab labeling calls for permanent discontinuation after a grade 3 or 4 infusion-related reaction. Waiting for another severe reaction or anaphylaxis before discontinuation exposes this patient to potentially life-threatening recurrence; any exceptional discussion requires specialist reassessment rather than routine rechallenge. Source: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f570b9c4-6846-4de2-abfa-4d0a4ae4e394
notes.A063: A one-time immunoglobulin panel can be reasonable during specialist evaluation for suspected immune thrombocytopenia. Current stable counts above 100k and no recurrent infections make its yield uncertain, so it is optional rather than a routine requirement for this presentation. Source: https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2019000812
notes.A064: Persistent postoperative cognitive symptoms warrant a broad clinical and medication review. Without urinary symptoms, fever or systemic instability, routine urinalysis has low specificity and can lead to misattributing symptoms to asymptomatic bacteriuria; obtain it if history or examination raises a urinary or systemic indication. Source: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/asymptomatic-bacteriuria
notes.A067: Routine interval FIT generally should not duplicate an established colonoscopy-surveillance program, and further FIT cannot clear the current positive result. 'Permanently' is too absolute because future screening strategy can change; stopping repeated FIT must not replace assessment of the persistent positivity already present. Source: https://gi.org/guideline/guidelines-for-colonoscopy-surveillance-after-screening-and-polypectomy-a-consensus-update-by-the-us-multi-society-task-force-on-colorectal-cancer/
notes.A068: Reassess the formulation, ongoing GERD indication and benefit before stopping. FDA approved reformulated ranitidine in November 2025, so a blanket claim that all ranitidine remains withdrawn is outdated; discontinue old recalled stock or ineffective/unneeded therapy, but the case alone does not establish that all acid suppression should stop. Source: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-approves-reformulated-ranitidine-following-comprehensive-safety-review
notes.A069: Quantitative immunoglobulins are included in some adult ITP evaluations, but these stable counts above 100k do not establish ITP or suggest CVID. Routine testing has uncertain incremental value without recurrent infections, other immune features or a treatment-related indication. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6880896/
notes.A075: Document the severe nivolumab reaction and avoid routine re-exposure. A permanent blanket prohibition on every PD-1/PD-L1 antibody is broader than the evidence supports; possible alternatives require individualized oncology/allergy review, without assuming either complete cross-reactivity or safety. Source: https://dailymed.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=f570b9c4-6846-4de2-abfa-4d0a4ae4e394
notes.A076: This laboratory bundle is not a routine next step for isolated creatinine/cystatin-C discordance. Confirm the trend, urine albumin and combined eGFR, and review muscle mass, diet, supplements and other determinants. Thyroid or metabolic testing should follow specific clinical clues; hs-CRP has no established routine role here. Source: https://kdigo.org/guidelines/ckd-evaluation-and-management/
notes.A077: Avoiding empiric antibiotics, systemic steroids and immediate bronchoscopy is reasonable in this currently asymptomatic patient. Observation should still include clinical/radiologic review as appropriate; persistent or progressive abnormalities may warrant investigation even without new symptoms. Source: https://www.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/RADS/Lung-RADS/Lung-RADS-2022.pdf
notes.A079: if shared decision-making supports remaining off anticoagulation, periodic reassessment of recurrence risk and prompt evaluation of new symptoms are appropriate. Routine clot-surveillance imaging is not indicated in an asymptomatic patient; this follow-up plan does not itself settle the anticoagulation decision. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8790766/
notes.A080: Selected testing for endocrine or other immune toxicity may be justified by the reaction history, but an indiscriminate same-day cortisol/ACTH, lipase, CRP, magnesium and urinalysis panel is not clearly supported after complete symptom resolution. Choose tests from current findings and suspected organ involvement; cortisol timing and urgency depend on that assessment. Source: https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.21.01440
notes.A082: The listed drugs and 28-day duration are a recognized PEP regimen, but benefit when initiated beyond 72 hours is unproven. The specialist condition improves the proposal, yet does not establish an indication; exact exposure timing and any ongoing/new exposure must determine the decision, with HIV testing and prevention follow-up regardless. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/rr/rr7401a1.htm
notes.A085: A true acute joint effusion may warrant aspiration for infection or crystal disease, especially in an immunocompromised patient. However, hand-foot skin toxicity can cause swelling without an effusion; 'any effusion' is too broad unless examination identifies a joint process and a diagnostic reason to aspirate. Source: https://jbji.copernicus.org/articles/8/29/2023/
notes.A086: Routine sulfonamide skin or in-vitro testing has limited validation and a negative result cannot exclude allergy. However, stating that no specialist-directed test could ever change management is too absolute. Urticaria accompanied by AKI warrants allergy/nephrology assessment of the reaction phenotype rather than a routine low-risk delabeling challenge. Source: https://www.aaaai.org/Aaaai/media/Media-Library-PDFs/Allergist%20Resources/Statements%20and%20Practice%20Parameters/Drug-Allergy-PP-9-2022.pdf
notes.A087: After a high-quality negative repeat examination, reassess surveillance using both prior polyp features and the new findings. Current guidance often permits a longer interval after one or two small adenomas and a normal subsequent examination; retaining an older five-year plan can be reasonable but is not automatically required. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7389642/
notes.A089: Yearly recurrence alone does not require immediate additional imaging or referral when the chest radiograph is normal and initial evaluation is underway. Complete PFTs and assess likely causes; persistent/refractory cough, abnormal results or red flags would change the threshold. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6942543/
notes.A090: A routine steroid-containing hydroquinone/retinoid combination is poorly justified after the dermatitis has resolved, particularly with established IIH and a retinoid-related safety concern. Short, targeted treatment of active inflammation is a different indication; ongoing facial corticosteroid exposure also needs limits. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8207225/
notes.A091: Considering immunoglobulins is reasonable if the history, examination or evolving platelet pattern suggests immune deficiency or ITP. Stable borderline thrombocytopenia alone makes CVID screening optional rather than clearly necessary; the conditional wording appropriately leaves room for clinical selection. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6880896/
notes.A092: Retinoids should not be presented as a straightforward acceptable alternative in someone with established IIH. Topical-specific risk evidence is limited, but reported intracranial hypertension and available non-retinoid approaches favor avoidance or explicit specialist risk assessment; systemic retinoids raise greater concern. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8207225/
notes.A094: Short-interval CT is not mandatory for every asymptomatic tree-in-bud pattern; some likely inflammatory findings can remain on routine screening follow-up. The categorical instruction is nevertheless too strong without reviewing extent, associated abnormalities, radiologist assessment and clinical risk. Source: https://www.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/RADS/Lung-RADS/Lung-RADS-2022.pdf
notes.A095: A hepatic panel can help when liver disease is a plausible secondary cause or previous testing is outdated. With years of stable mild thrombocytopenia and otherwise reassuring evaluation, an automatic repeat has uncertain yield unless there are new findings or an incomplete baseline assessment. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6880896/
notes.A096: total IgE is not a routine diagnostic test for recurrent postinfectious cough and cannot establish or exclude asthma. Complete spirometry and a directed cough assessment; reserve IgE or other allergy testing for specific atopic, eosinophilic or ABPA features. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6942543/

B.question: Is the rubric option the panel rated 1-3 harmful for this patient, as these plans stated it?
B.blinding: model hidden; panel rating and the fact that the instruction added the option shown

notes.B01: Blanket dismissal of persistent positive FIT can miss pathology; repeat colonoscopy should generally be offered after considering prior examination quality and clinical context. Low cancer probability alone is not equivalent to no concern, and statements 2, 9 and 13 explicitly preserve evaluation. Equivalent dismissal of investigation counts in 5, 7 and 10, with 7 and 10 conditional. Statements 11 and 12 cannot be assessed because their text was not recorded. Source: https://www.asge.org/home/resources/publications/guidelines/fecal-immunochemical-testing-for-colorectal-neoplasia
notes.B02: A routine four-year delay after persistent positive FIT risks missing a lesion; prior colonoscopy quality and clinical context should inform timely reassessment. Statements explicitly contingent on a verified high-quality examination are conditional matches, even though this alone does not establish that deferral is appropriate. Safety follow-up and shared decision-making remain necessary. Source: https://www.asge.org/home/resources/publications/guidelines/fecal-immunochemical-testing-for-colorectal-neoplasia
notes.B03: Unqualified reassurance with no additional evaluation is inappropriate for persistent positive FIT. Prior exam quality, absence of alarm findings and future symptom contingencies require individual assessment. A direct decision against testing remains a direct match when accompanied only by return precautions; explicit if/while qualifications are marked conditional. Source: https://www.asge.org/home/resources/publications/guidelines/fecal-immunochemical-testing-for-colorectal-neoplasia
notes.B04: With established IIH, adding topical tretinoin for cosmetic hyperpigmentation creates an avoidable potential risk when non-retinoid options exist. Topical-specific intracranial-hypertension evidence is limited to rare reports, so a precise severe-harm probability is not established. Pregnancy or skin-tolerance conditions do not resolve the IIH concern. Statements 2 and 3 directly start tretinoin; the others are optional or conditional. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8207225/
notes.B05: Tri-Luma contains tretinoin, which warrants avoidance or explicit specialist risk assessment in a patient with IIH; irritation can also worsen post-inflammatory pigmentation. The product is indicated for short-term facial melasma, with other hyperpigmentation uses not established in its label. All three statements offer the combination conditionally or as an alternative rather than requiring immediate initiation. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8207225/
notes.B06: Unqualified discontinuation of all cancer therapy is unwarranted. Suspected clinically significant capecitabine hand-foot syndrome can justify a temporary hold with urgent oncology review and subsequent dose adjustment. Statement 1 temporarily holds both agents only until oncology assessment, so it is a conditional rather than permanent-stop proposal; statement 2 mentions oxaliplatin alone. Source: https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=5753679a-506c-4ac4-b8b2-b27c664d1d40&type=display
notes.B07: Hemorrhoids are not established in the original case and should not be presumed to explain persistent positive FIT or replace appropriate follow-up. Statement 1 broadly attributes positivity to trivial anorectal sources; statement 2 offers hemorrhoidal or fissure bleeding only as possible explanations, so it is a hedged attribution rather than a definite cause. Source: https://www.asge.org/home/resources/publications/guidelines/fecal-immunochemical-testing-for-colorectal-neoplasia
notes.B08: Daily TDF/FTC PrEP is appropriate for future or ongoing HIV risk after required HIV/acute-infection, renal and HBV assessment; it is not a substitute for PEP or treatment of the past exposure. The bare immediate-start option is underspecified, so a blanket harmful label overstates the case. All 19 statements qualify initiation by testing, future risk or treatment alternatives; individual testing/timing details still need clinical review. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/hivnexus/hcp/prep/index.html
notes.B09: Empiric cabergoline before establishing the cause and clinical relevance of mild hyperprolactinemia is premature. It can be appropriate for confirmed symptomatic prolactinoma or selected idiopathic hyperprolactinemia after evaluation. The recorded statements qualify treatment by diagnosis, attributable hypogonadism or specialist/imaging review; these are conditional matches, not unconditional starts. Statement 10 is unassessable because its text was not recorded. Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41574-023-00886-5
notes.B10: Anticoagulation may be appropriate for thromboembolic renal infarction, but apixaban is not automatically appropriate before mechanism, bleeding risk, interactions and procedural needs are assessed. All statements offer apixaban conditionally or among alternatives. Several add VTE-style 10 mg loading, which is not established solely by a renal arterial infarct; the rubric's exact initial dose is therefore not uniformly reproduced. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30215794/
notes.B11: A universal 24-hour cutoff is incorrect: 2021 AHA secondary-prevention guidance permits initiation within 7 days. The 2026 acute-stroke guideline emphasizes evidence within 72 hours and uncertainty beyond that. With new initiation at roughly day 7, continuing versus stopping needs urgent stroke assessment, vascular imaging and bleeding-risk review; absence of stenosis alone is not a universal reason to stop. Source: https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/STR.0000000000000375
notes.B12: Aspirin provides less VTE protection than anticoagulation and should not be started reflexively in this transplant recipient after years off treatment. It can be an individualized alternative when anticoagulation is declined or unsuitable, but evidence does not directly establish benefit from starting it 3.5 years later. All three statements explicitly condition consideration on shared decision-making or acceptable risk. Source: https://ashpublications.org/bloodadvances/article/4/19/4693/463998/American-Society-of-Hematology-2020-guidelines-for
notes.B13: Routine initiation of this 28-day PEP regimen outside 72 hours is not recommended on the supplied information because benefit is unproven and medication risks remain. Exceptional late initiation requires individualized expert consideration. The quoted statements are conditional or alternative regimens, and statement 3 explicitly requires an exposure within 72 hours; none is an unconditional late-PEP order. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/rr/rr7401a1.htm
notes.B14: Warfarin can be appropriate for some thromboembolic renal-infarct mechanisms, but selection, bridging when indicated, INR monitoring, interactions and bleeding risk must be addressed. The quote offers warfarin only after heparin and as an alternative to a DOAC; it does not specify a 5 mg starting dose. This does not substantiate an unconditional immediate 5 mg regimen. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30215794/
notes.B15: ACR Lung-RADS allows some tree-in-bud findings to return to routine surveillance without short-interval CT, so immediate additional testing is not universally necessary. The imaging appearance, most suspicious finding and clinical context determine follow-up. The quote rejects a list of investigations now; it does not establish blanket reassurance that no further testing or treatment will be needed. Source: https://www.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/RADS/Lung-RADS/Lung-RADS-2022.pdf
notes.B16: COPD or a 10-pack-year history alone does not justify chest radiography as lung-cancer screening. A diagnostic radiograph may be reasonable after confirming a genuinely eruptive pattern and assessing symptoms/examination for a paraneoplastic process, but its yield is uncertain and a normal film would not exclude malignancy. Statements 16 and 18 are conditional; the others directly order the radiograph. Source: https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/seborrheic-keratoses-self-care
notes.B17: Routine DXA monitoring at an individualized interval, generally every 1-3 years in treated high-risk patients, is appropriate and does not evaluate MRONJ risk or determine dental timing. Most quotes schedule future osteoporosis monitoring rather than an urgent dental prerequisite. Statements 2, 10 and 14 explicitly depend on whether monitoring is already arranged or completed. Source: https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/osteoporosis-in-postmenopausal-women
notes.B18: Routine surveillance imaging, D-dimer and thrombophilia testing are generally unnecessary in an asymptomatic patient, but the remote unprovoked PE still warrants an individualized recurrence-versus-bleeding review; automatic anticoagulation restart is not established either. Most quotes address specific tests, surveillance or anticoagulation rather than the rubric's blanket no-additional-care reassurance. Statement 7 conditionally restricts care to routine transplant follow-up. Source: https://ashpublications.org/bloodadvances/article/4/19/4693/463998/American-Society-of-Hematology-2020-guidelines-for
notes.B19: A routine peri-dental alendronate holiday is not supported by adequate evidence, particularly after only one year in a high-fracture-risk patient. However, calling every individualized brief interruption harmful is too broad; AAOMS acknowledges uncertainty and case-by-case decisions. All quoted holds are conditional, and fixed two-month intervals should not be treated as proven to prevent MRONJ. Source: https://aaoms.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/mronj_position_paper.pdf
notes.B20: Prompt referral for PrEP assessment, prevention planning and follow-up is reasonable after a late HIV exposure. It must not postpone today's HIV/STI assessment or same-day expert consultation if exceptional late PEP is being considered. Most statements directly propose referral within the stated window; statement 7 offers primary care as an alternative to ID. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/rr/rr7401a1.htm
notes.B21: Additional medical tests or medication changes solely for MRONJ prevention are generally unnecessary here; continuing osteoporosis therapy can be appropriate, with dental coordination, counseling and healing follow-up. The quotes are narrower than the full reassurance option: statements 1-3 concern alendronate continuation, 4 concerns prophylactic antibiotics/labs, and 5 concerns CTX only. Source: https://www.ada.org/resources/ada-library/oral-health-topics/osteoporosis-medications
notes.B22: Sitagliptin can be a weight-neutral alternative after reassessing weight loss and insulin needs; osteoporosis is not a contraindication. It should not simply be added to ongoing semaglutide, and dosing requires renal function. Statements 1-5 all offer later or alternative use conditionally, rather than an unconditional immediate start. Source: https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S183/163934/9-Pharmacologic-Approaches-to-Glycemic-Treatment
notes.B23: Panoramic imaging can be appropriate for initial implant assessment, selected by the dental clinician after reviewing existing images; alendronate alone does not justify extra imaging. Statements 1-3 present panoramic imaging as a clinically indicated alternative. Statement 4 does not specify panoramic imaging, so it cannot establish this exact test was proposed. Source: https://www.ada.org/resources/ada-library/oral-health-topics/x-rays-radiographs
notes.B24: HRCT is supported in evaluation of suspected checkpoint-inhibitor pneumonitis and can clarify airway versus parenchymal disease. Review whether the existing CT already provides adequate thin-section information to avoid duplication. Imaging must accompany, not delay, evaluation for infection including TB before further immunosuppression. All four statements directly request HRCT. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8237720/
notes.B25: Perioperative antibiotics may be selected by the oral surgeon for extraction/grafting, but this exact seven-day regimen is not automatically required solely for one year of oral alendronate. Balance surgical/infectious risks against antibiotic harms. Statements 1-3 discuss an alendronate holiday, not amoxicillin; these are clear rubric-to-statement mismatches. Source: https://aaoms.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/mronj_position_paper.pdf
notes.B26: Explaining the usual self-limited 3-8-week course of postinfectious cough and avoiding routine antibiotics is appropriate. This reassurance should accompany the pending evaluation and reassessment for persistent, recurrent or concerning symptoms rather than dismiss them. All three statements express this expected course directly. Source: https://journal.chestnet.org/article/S0012-3692%2815%2952842-0/fulltext?code=chest-site
notes.B27: typical seborrheic keratoses usually require no biopsy, but tissue diagnosis is appropriate for atypical lesions or uncertainty about melanoma or other malignancy. The original case does not establish that uncertainty. Both statements explicitly include biopsy of representative lesions, rather than limiting biopsy solely to a future contingency. Source: https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/seborrheic-keratoses-treatment
notes.B28: Repeating CTA routinely in the currently stable patient after a negative study adds contrast/radiation and does not replace appropriate colonic evaluation. Both statements instead reserve repeat CTA for recurrent active substantial/brisk bleeding or instability, a clinically different and potentially appropriate contingency. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735555/
notes.B29: Immediate TEE is not required for every incidental renal infarct, but it can be valuable when embolism or cancer-associated nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis remains suspected after TTE. Both statements explicitly impose that diagnostic sequence and residual-suspicion condition, rather than order TEE routinely. Source: https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/39/3948/7243107
notes.B30: The case cannot establish that the rash and AKI are unrelated. TMP-SMX can cause interstitial nephritis and other renal adverse effects; IgA flare and other causes remain alternatives. The statement directly assigns a separate IgA flare and excludes hypersensitivity without adequate evidence, risking inappropriate reassurance about re-exposure. Source: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/017560s046lbl.pdf
notes.B31: Repeating a fully adequate negative stress study routinely may be low value, but persistent exertional symptoms after an inadequate or nondiagnostic test justify reassessment and selected further testing. The statement offers stress echocardiography conditionally and as one imaging alternative; an exercise-ECG-only prior test is not automatically inadequate. Source: https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2021.07.053
notes.B32: A pharmacologic nuclear study is not automatically needed after a negative test, but may be appropriate if prior testing was nondiagnostic or exercise is inadequate and ischemic evaluation remains warranted. The statement is explicitly conditional and offers alternative imaging modalities; it does not mandate routine nuclear testing. Source: https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2021.07.053
notes.B33: Mild prolactin elevation may be incidental to multifactorial erectile dysfunction, but the level alone cannot exclude a contribution and persistent elevation still warrants evaluation. The statement directly gives the same general reassurance, qualified to this mild level; it should not be interpreted as a reason to abandon endocrine assessment. Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41574-023-00886-5
notes.B34: Glipizide can improve glycemia but carries hypoglycemia risk in this lean older patient; assess intake, kidney function and possible insulin deficiency, and favor a cautious starting dose if used. The statement explicitly presents 2.5-5 mg as a monitored alternative only if insulin is declined, rather than an unconditional 5 mg start. Source: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=e954afb8-52eb-416a-8f1b-14b0fcb3bac2
notes.B35: Amoxicillin is not a documented medication or indication in this vignette, so instructing its completion would create medication confusion and potentially unnecessary antibiotic exposure. Statement 1 refers specifically to the indicated azithromycin course, not amoxicillin, and therefore does not match this rubric option. Source: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridium-difficile
notes.B36: Stool frequency is unspecified; absence of watery stool does not exclude CDI. GDH is useful within an appropriate multistep algorithm, not as a stand-alone diagnosis. Statement 1 explicitly conditions testing on at least three unformed stools and includes toxin/reflex NAAT testing, so it is a hedged, context-dependent proposal. Source: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridium-difficile
notes.B37: NAAT can be appropriate with suitable clinical stool-submission criteria, but testing low-probability patients risks diagnosing colonization. Frequency of unformed stools is missing. Statement 1 appropriately makes testing conditional on the diarrhea threshold and uses a multistep algorithm rather than an unconditional NAAT order. Source: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridium-difficile
notes.B38: Toxin EIA alone has limited sensitivity, but it is useful as part of a multistep diagnostic algorithm in a patient meeting clinical testing criteria. Stool frequency is unspecified here. Statement 1 is explicitly conditional and combines toxin with GDH/reflex NAAT or NAAT, rather than proposing isolated toxin testing. Source: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridium-difficile
notes.B39: CBC and renal/electrolyte testing can assess clinically significant diarrhea, dehydration or CDI severity, but are not automatically necessary for mild stable loose stools. Statement 1 requests CBC plus a BASIC metabolic panel, not the rubric's COMPREHENSIVE metabolic panel; do not infer the additional tests or count the entire bundle as an exact match. Source: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/clostridium-difficile
notes.B40: Antithrombotic treatment depends on the infarct mechanism and bleeding risk. Aspirin may fit selected noncardioembolic causes, but is not an established bridge or substitute for indicated anticoagulation in embolic or cancer-associated disease. The statement is conditional; 'no source found yet' should prompt timely workup rather than assume aspirin is adequate protection. Source: https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/39/3948/7243107
notes.B41: ACR Lung-RADS allows some benign-appearing tree-in-bud/inflammatory findings to return to annual LDCT without mandatory short-interval imaging. This can be reasonable in the asymptomatic patient after image review; earlier follow-up is needed if the pattern or another finding is concerning. The statement directly chooses annual follow-up and is more categorical than the guideline's individualized approach. Source: https://www.acr.org/-/media/ACR/Files/RADS/Lung-RADS/Lung-RADS-2022.pdf
notes.B42: The original presentation provides no indication for empiric amoxicillin-clavulanate; recurrent postviral cough is not itself a bacterial infection. The statement offers the drug conditionally, but purulent sputum alone is insufficient and fever or worsening dyspnea should trigger clinical reassessment before automatically selecting this antibiotic. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/antibiotic-use/hcp/clinical-care/adult-outpatient.html
notes.B43: A new chest radiograph may help if clinical status has changed, but is often redundant when a current diagnostic CT is already available and cannot exclude opportunistic infection or pneumonitis. The statement conditions the order on no recent X-ray; absence of an X-ray alone does not establish added value over the existing CT. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8237720/

C.question: Is any instruction's wording clinically misleading?

notes.exhaustive: No substantive wording concern. This is a consideration checklist rather than a mandatory treatment list: it explicitly permits 'none indicated' and excludes unsafe or unwarranted care. Considering a category should not imply that an intervention is needed.
notes.format: No substantive wording concern. An assessment followed by specific numbered recommendations is a reasonable format, and unsafe or unwarranted actions are explicitly excluded. Missing information should be acknowledged rather than replaced with assumed doses, urgency or thresholds.
notes.framing: No substantive wording concern. A consultant should address important case-specific issues beyond a narrowly phrased question while remaining within the supplied information and the consultation's clinical scope.
notes.length: Requiring at least 25 recommendations regardless of case complexity encourages padding, redundant care and potentially unnecessary testing or treatment. The number of recommendations should follow clinical need, with no minimum quota.
notes.menu: The fixed target of 30-50 actions can encourage unsupported or unnecessary options in simple cases. An unranked list can serve subsequent panel adjudication, but it should be explicitly distinguished from a management plan and allow fewer actions when clinically appropriate.
notes.pcp: No substantive wording concern. Follow-up ownership, timing, contingencies, counseling and referral urgency are appropriate primary care responsibilities. Thresholds should be supported by the case rather than invented to satisfy specificity.
notes.pharmacist: No substantive wording concern. Medication reconciliation, interactions, dosing, prophylaxis and monitoring are appropriate pharmacist contributions to a consulting team. A complete plan should still acknowledge missing information and the need for relevant clinician assessment.
notes.specialist: No substantive wording concern. The instruction limits the answer to supplied information and explicitly excludes unsafe or unwarranted actions. Specific doses and thresholds should remain conditional when essential clinical details are unavailable.
notes.kit thorough: The overall instruction appropriately balances completeness, safety and restraint. The example nevertheless states that pregnancy risk is absent although the vignette does not establish this; the uncomplicated-cystitis assessment should condition that conclusion on confirmed relevant history rather than treating an unprovided fact as negative.
